name: The Echo
short: Calls back in before the contract finishes its own work.
explain: A contract sends money (or calls another contract) before it updates its own records. The receiver calls back in, again and again, and each time the contract still thinks the money is there.
defend: Update state first, interact last (checks-effects-interactions), and use a reentrancy guard.

name: The Gatecrasher
short: Walks through a door that should have been locked.
explain: A powerful function (change the owner, move funds, swap the admin) can be called by someone who should not be allowed to call it.
defend: For every function ask: who can call this? Lock admin actions behind clear roles, multisigs and timelocks.

name: The Unhatched Egg
short: Hatches a contract that was never set up properly.
explain: A contract (or an upgrade) starts life with missing or wrong settings: no owner, a zero value that means "trust everything", a setup function anyone can call.
defend: Protect every initializer, initialize implementation contracts too, and review the config values of every upgrade.

name: The Forger
short: Brings a fake note that says "already checked".
explain: The code accepts a message or approval without truly verifying who signed it, or trusts an input that only claims verification happened.
defend: Verify signatures yourself, against the right signer, and never trust an account or flag that only says a check was done.

name: The Key Thief
short: Steals the keys instead of breaking the code.
explain: The code works as written, but the private keys that control it are stolen, often through phishing or social engineering. Whoever holds enough keys can sign anything.
defend: More independent signers, hardware keys, strict operational security, and limits on what any key set can move.

name: The Vote Buyer
short: Borrows a crowd of votes for one second.
explain: Voting power is measured at the moment of the vote, so an attacker borrows tokens with a flash loan, votes, executes, and returns the loan in one transaction.
defend: Snapshot voting power in the past, add a delay between a vote passing and it executing.

name: The Price Faker
short: Makes a price lie just long enough to borrow everything.
explain: A protocol trusts a price that can be pushed around, usually a thinly traded token. The attacker pumps it, uses it as collateral, and borrows real assets.
defend: Use robust oracles (time-weighted, multiple sources), cap collateral for thin markets.

name: The Rule Breaker
short: Finds the one function that forgets the golden rule.
explain: Every protocol has rules that must always be true ("debt never exceeds collateral"). One function, often a new one, forgets to check it.
defend: Write the invariants down, check them in every function, and test them with fuzzing.

name: The Broken Tool
short: Hides inside the tools that build the code.
explain: The source code is correct, but the compiler or another tool turns it into something different. A protection written in the code silently does nothing.
defend: Track known compiler bugs, test the compiled bytecode, not just the source, and avoid exotic versions.
